description_full: Vipshop Holdings Limited operates online platforms in the People's Republic of China. The company operates through Vip.com, Shan Shan Outlets, and Others segments. It provides womenswear, menswear, sportswear and sporting goods, baby and children products, shoes and bags, skincare and cosmetics, home goods and other lifestyle products, and supermarket and other products. The company also engages in warehousing, retail business, product procurement, and software development and information technology support activities. It provides branded products through its vip.com and vipshop.com online platforms, as well as through retail stores. Vipshop Holdings Limited was founded in 2008 and is headquartered in Guangzhou, the People's Republic of China.

financial_summary: Vipshop Holdings Limited is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $6.3B market cap on $15.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years and +9% annually across the full decade — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.

Returns on capital run at 55% against a 9% cost of capital — a 46-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 22% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $821M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.03× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 90× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 16.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 8% operating margin is roughly in line with the Consumer Cyclical median (7%).

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 32% over the past year excluding the latest month.

val: The stock trades 77% below its DCF fair value of $57.23, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 6%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $44.90 to $75.77 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Consumer Cyclical peers: P/E 4.5 vs 18.8 and P/FCF 7.7 vs 16.7 (sector median).

Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 13.0% (above the risk-free rate).
The 20 covering analysts target $15.86 on average, 20% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 55% clears the cost of capital of 8.9% by 46pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.61).
It runs a 22% gross margin and converts 5% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.03x.
ROE of 18% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.9x equity multiplier).
It spends 1.7% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $2.6B.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 3.4, in the safe zone).
It runs on negative working capital (-30 days), so customers and suppliers effectively fund its operations.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -1.4% over 3 years, -0.0% over 5 years and 8.7% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 15%).
At current returns, reinvesting 25% of profits supports about 13.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -11.3% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.3x, 1.9% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 3, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.5%), and institutions hold 64%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (10 sales, net $951K sold).
It returns 16.0% a year to shareholders (11.8% in buybacks and 4.7% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 5.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 15,145 employees, each generates about $1.0M of revenue, 2.7x the Consumer Cyclical median, and revenue has grown 8.7% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $54K of free cash flow per employee.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
